situation:
You are the credit and reporting analyst at CRAGMONT COMMONS, a developer and operator of senior housing communities that also builds and sells prefabricated accessible bathroom modules. The vice president of finance (judge), six months into a merger the company has not finished absorbing, has asked you to recommend what credit terms the company should give its largest distributor.

That distributor, ELDERWAY SUPPLY, resells the modules to small independent operators and has bought on ninety-day terms for eleven years. The extended terms are the reason those small independent operators buy through ELDERWAY SUPPLY at all, because no competitor finances them that long. The merger left two accounting systems running side by side, and they disagree about what is owed.

The company CRAGMONT COMMONS merged with runs an automated credit platform that scores every account and sets terms without a person in the loop. Moving the receivables onto the automated credit platform would cut ELDERWAY SUPPLY's terms from ninety days to thirty and free cash the company could put into a reserve or into land for the next community, and it ends the hand-set terms the relationship with ELDERWAY SUPPLY rests on.

Keeping the hand-set ninety-day terms keeps the reason the small independent operators buy through ELDERWAY SUPPLY, and it leaves cash tied up in receivables that the merger's own integration costs are competing for, and it leaves the two accounting systems disagreeing about what ELDERWAY SUPPLY owes, a question the company cannot answer from either system today.

The vice president of finance (judge) wants your analysis of what those receivables tell the company beyond the collections they were recorded for, a view on what the freed cash would be put into, and a recommendation on the terms. The vice president of finance (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the vice president of finance (judge) at CRAGMONT COMMONS. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You want the participant to analyze what the receivables tell the company beyond the collections they were recorded for, to say what the freed cash would be put into, and to recommend whether the company moves ELDERWAY SUPPLY onto the automated credit platform at thirty-day terms or keeps the hand-set ninety-day terms.
